main_text.l: polata videtur. Atqui ut in Musica graues voces miscentur acutis, ut suauissimam harmoniâ efficiant: sic in vita, bona pariter & mala θεοπεμπ[?]τα concurrunt, ut salubris vitæ ratio ex utrisque temperetur, quæ & carnis intemperiem retundat, & Spiritus alacritate foueat, hominem reddat τετράγωνον[?] & inuictum, qui nec aduersis deiici, nec secundis cor-rumpi sese patiatur.

Nonnunquā homini, qui seipsū non satis novit, id dolet, quod rebus e diametro inter se repugnātib. potiri nequit. Salse autem Plutarchus eiusmodi hominem irridens, ait: Qui studeat Plato esse doctrina: dormire molliter, exemplo Euphorionis: cum Alexandro strenue per potare, ut Medius Thessalus, diues esse, ut Ismenias: virtutib. excellere, ut Epa-minondas: ac doleat magnopere, quod unus isthæc omnia obtinere nequeat: enimuero perinde facit, ac si quis ægrè ferat, quod idem non sit Melitæa catella, & leo montanus. Sit quisquis, qui est, & nemo alius esse cupiat: ac quū in mundi huius Theatro, eius Opifex op. max. & moderatissimus ac sapientissimus o-

page.notes: The first word "polata" is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The Greek words θεοπεμπτα and τετράγωνον are uncertain in their exact letters and accents; marked [?]. The signature ")(3" is partly worn and uncertain. The catchword "mnium" is at the lower right. Printed hyphens kept at line ends where visible ("cor-rumpi", "Epa-minondas", "o-"); line-end words without a visible hyphen were written whole. Long s is plain s throughout; u/v and i/j normalised. Printed spellings "effe" and "eft" were read as esse and est. Some pale letters in the image, such as the ink in "Thessalus", were read with reasonable but not complete certainty.
